cases.sentence: У дверей, над криво прибитою визитною карточкой, виднелась ручка колокольчика, и в передней встретила пришедших какая-то не то служанка, не то компаньонка в чепце – явные признаки ___ хозяйки.
cases.explain: «прогрессивных стремлений» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The villa in which Avdotia, or Evdoksia, Nikitishna Kukshin resided was one of the usual Moscow pattern, and stood in one of the recently consumed streets (for as we know, every fifth year sees each of our provincial capitals burnt to the ground) of the town of ——. Beside the front door there hung (over a cracked, crooked visiting-card) a bell-handle, while in the hall the visitors were met by a female who constituted, not exactly a maidservant, but a mob-capped "lady companion." And it need hardly be added that these two phenomena, the bell-handle and the "lady companion," constituted clear evidence of the "progressiveness" of the hostess's views.

cases.sentence: – Это вы, Victor? – раздался ___ из соседней комнаты. – Войдите.
cases.explain: «тонкий голос» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: On Sitnikov inquiring whether Avdotia Nikitishna were within, a shrill voice interrupted him from an adjoining room:

cases.sentence: – Это вы, Victor? – раздался тонкий голос из ___. – Войдите.
cases.explain: «соседней комнаты» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On Sitnikov inquiring whether Avdotia Nikitishna were within, a shrill voice interrupted him from an adjoining room:

cases.sentence: – Я не один, – промолвил Ситников, лихо скидывая свою венгерку, под которою оказалось нечто вроде поддевки или пальто-сака, и бросая ___ Аркадию и Базарову.
cases.explain: «бойкий взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The female in the mob-cap disappeared. "I have not come alone," Sitnikov responded as, after an inquiring glance at Arkady and Bazarov, he divested himself of his greatcoat, and revealed thereunder a sort of sack jacket.

cases.sentence: Комната, в которой они очутились, походила скорее на ___, чем на гостиную.
cases.explain: «рабочий кабинет» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The young men did as bidden, and found themselves in a room which resembled a workshop rather than a parlour. On tables were piled promiscuous papers, letters and Russian magazines (most of the latter uncut); everywhere on the floor were to be seen gleaming the fag-ends of cigarettes; and on a leather-padded sofa a lady—youngish, flaxen-haired, and clad in a négligée soiled silk gown—was lolling in a semi-recumbent position. About her stumpy wrists were clasped a large pair of bracelets, and over her head was thrown a lace mantilla. Rising, she draped her shoulders carelessly in a velvet tippet with faded ermine trimming, and, saying indolently, "Good day, Victor," pressed Sitnikov's hand.

cases.sentence: Бумаги, письма, толстые нумера ___, большею частью неразрезанные, валялись по запыленным столам; везде белели разбросанные окурки папирос.
cases.explain: «русских журналов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The young men did as bidden, and found themselves in a room which resembled a workshop rather than a parlour. cases.sentence: В маленькой и невзрачной фигурке ___ не было ничего безобразного; но выражение ее лица неприятно действовало на зрителя.
cases.explain: «эманципированной женщины» — after the preposition «в», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: That said, she pressed his hand even as she had done Sitnikov's. Bazarov frowned, for though the plain, insignificant features of the emancipated lady contained nothing actually to repel, there was something in their mien which produced upon the beholder the sort of unpleasant impression which might have inclined him to ask her: "Are you hungry, or bored, or afraid? At all events, what is it you want?" Also, like Sitnikov, she kept pawing the air as she spoke, and her every word, her every gesture, revealed such a lack of control as at times amounted to sheer awkwardness. In short, though she conceived herself to be just a simple, good-hearted creature, her bearing was of the kind to lead the beholder to reflect that, no matter what she did, it was not what she had intended to do, and that everything was done (to use the children's term) "on purpose"—that is to say, non-simply and non-naturally.

cases.sentence: (За ней водилась привычка, свойственная многим провинциальным и московским дамам, – с ___ знакомства звать мужчин по фамилии.) – Хотите сигару?
cases.explain: «первого дня» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "Yes, I have met you before, Bazarov," she repeated (like many other contemporary females of Moscow and the provinces, she had adopted the fashion of calling men by their surnames alone on first introduction). "Will you have a cigar?"

cases.sentence: (Когда она смеялась, ее ___ обнажалась над зубами.) – Не правда ли, Базаров, он сибарит?
cases.explain: «верхняя десна» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "You Sybarite!" exclaimed Evdoksia with a smile (a smile always brought her upper gum prominently into view). "Is he not, Bazarov?"

cases.sentence: – Ну нет, – возразил Базаров, – кусок мяса лучше куска хлеба, даже с ___ зрения.
cases.explain: «химической точки» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "No, I do not," he replied. "On the contrary, I think that, even from the chemical point of view, a piece of meat is better than a piece of bread."

cases.sentence: Кстати, читали вы статью Кислякова о ___ в «Московских ведомостях»?
cases.explain: «женском труде» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: "Yes, I. And please guess its use. It is for making unbreakable dolls and pipe-bowls. You see that, like yourself, I am of a practical turn of mind. But, as yet, I have not completed my course of study. It still remains for me to read up my Liebig. Apropos, have you seen an article in the Viedomosti on Woman's Work—an article by Kisliakov? If not, you should read it (for I presume that you take an interest in the Feminine Question, and also in the Question of the Schools?). But what is your friend's line? Apropos, what is his name?"

cases.sentence: – Вы ___; вы такой критик.
cases.explain: «опасный господин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "Because you are a dangerous gentleman—you are a critic so caustic that in your presence my confusion leads me to begin speaking like a lady-landowner of the Steppes. Apropos, I am a lady-landowner myself; for, though I employ a local steward named Erothei (a sort of Cooper's 'Pathfinder,' but compounded with a blend of independence in his composition), I retain the ultimate reins of management in my own hands. But how unbearable this town is!—yes, even though I have made it my permanent home, seeing that nothing else was to be done!"

cases.sentence: Я сама имением управляю, и, представьте, у меня староста Ерофей – ___, точно Патфайндер[72] Купера: что-то такое в нем непосредственное!
cases.explain: «удивительный тип» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "Because you are a dangerous gentleman—you are a critic so caustic that in your presence my confusion leads me to begin speaking like a lady-landowner of the Steppes. cases.sentence: – Все такие ___, вот что ужасно!
cases.explain: «мелкие интересы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "But its interests are so petty!" continued Evdoksia. "That is what troubles me. Once upon a time I used to winter in Moscow, but now good Monsieur Kukshin has to dwell there alone. And Moscow itself is, is—well, not what it used to be. As a matter of fact, I contemplate going abroad. I have spent the whole year in making my preparations for the journey."

cases.sentence: – Есть здесь ___? – спросил Базаров, допивая третью рюмку.
cases.explain: «хорошенькие женщины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "Have you any good-looking ladies in this town?" Bazarov asked after a third glassful of champagne.

cases.explain: «хорошеньких женщинах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: "Of the smart women of the day."

cases.sentence: – Я ___ не разделяю; я имею свои.
cases.explain: «ничьих мнений» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "I agree with no man's opinions," he remarked. "I have some of my own."

cases.sentence: – Не за бабенок, а за права женщин, которые я поклялась защищать до ___ крови.
cases.explain: «последней капли» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "I am not defending them at all," said Madame Kukshin. "I am merely standing up for the rights of women—rights which I have sworn to defend to the last drop of my blood."

cases.sentence: – Плетка дело доброе, – заметил Базаров, – только мы вот добрались до ___…
cases.explain: «последней капли» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "But you are a Slavophil: you believe in the principles of the Domostroi,[3] and would like always to be holding over women a scourge."

cases.sentence: Наступило ___.
cases.explain: «внезапное молчание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: There fell a sudden silence.

cases.sentence: – А это заведение твоего отца тоже ___? – промолвил Базаров, ткнув пальцем на кабак, мимо которого они в это мгновение проходили.
cases.explain: «нравственное явление» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Sitnikov vented another of his shrill giggles. But, being also ashamed of his origin, he felt at a loss whether to plume himself upon, or to take offence at, Bazarov's unexpected pleasantry.

cases.sentence: Он очень стыдился своего происхождения и не знал, чувствовать ли ему себя польщенным или обиженным от ___ Базарова.
cases.explain: «неожиданного тыканья» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: [1] Robert Wilhelm Bunsen (1811-1899), chemist and physicist; inventor of Bunsen's burner and magnesium light; and originator (with Kirchhov) of spectrum analysis. [2] Pierre Joseph Proudhon (1809-1865), a French doctrinaire who taught that anarchy is the culmination of all social progress. [3] A curious old sixteenth-century work which, usually attributed to the monk Sylvester, purports to be a "guide to household management," and, incidentally, gives a terrible picture of the power of the Russian husband over his wife. [4] Louise Michel (1830-1906), a French anarchist long resident in London.
